bullets: tizujccrTvE game 5 of 8 (video 901-1112s), a win in overtime against a Golem/Wizard beatdown deck after regulation finished 1-1.

Two cheap win conditions carried all the damage: a Goblin Barrel at clock 2:04 took the enemy left tower 4858 -> 4171, and an Evolution Goblin Barrel plus Evolution Wall Breakers push at clock 1:04-1:03 took the enemy right tower 4335 -> 527 and destroyed it.

With no big spell in the list, defence is layered cheap cards: Royal Delivery on air (clock 2:42 onto a Baby Dragon), Magic Archer on stacked columns (clock 2:20), Fire Spirit held specifically for the opponent's hero ability ("we have the fire spirit ready for the ability", 967s), and Tesla plus Skeletons plus Wall Breakers to bleed a Golem push (clock 0:42-0:15).

The Ronin is played centrally as a defensive mini-tank, not at the bridge (tiles [8, 10], [1, 11], [3, 10]), and spaced away from his own barrel so one Wizard splash cannot hit both — "now the Ronan is just staying far away from the wizard so it doesn't splash the barrel" (1015-1019s).

Its weakness showed at clock 0:08: the deck has no hard Golem answer, and the push took his left tower — "wait, what? My tower is gone" (1066-1068s). He converted the overtime free half into two more barrels and a Wall Breakers pair, closing on a cycle count: "he has no barbarian barrel in cycle and he can't fully defend a barrel unless he lightnings it at this point" (1095-1099s).

Magic Archer placement is spell-aware throughout: he put it at tile [9, 0] in front of his own King Tower at clock 1:20 rather than commit it forward, because he could not rule out Lightning, Fireball or Vines.

new_deck.display_name: Ronin Goblin Barrel Wall Breakers double bait
new_deck.rationale: Two cheap spell-bait win conditions (Goblin Barrel and Wall Breakers) plus a swarm of 1-elixir bait cards at a 2.9 average, backed by Tesla and Royal Delivery on defence.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: Goblin Barrel and Wall Breakers are two independent win conditions that demand different answers, so a single small spell can never cover both — in this match the opponent's one Barbarian Barrel was, in Ryley's words, "definitely the best play he could have made", and the moment it left his cycle the game was decided. The 2.9-elixir curve lets it out-cycle heavy decks: Skeletons, Fire Spirit and Wall Breakers all cost 1-2 and double as defensive kite pieces, so chip pressure never stops for defence. Ronin is the deck's only real mini-tank and is used centrally on defence, where his parry punishes melee attackers; Tesla and Royal Delivery cover the buildings-and-air holes that a barrel deck otherwise has. The deck has no big spell, which is a deliberate trade — Ryley's Magic Archer placements are chosen around the opponent's possible Lightning or Fireball rather than around trading spells.
